text: Agmatine can leave you flat and numb, which people do report even though the human trials only found stomach problems. So stop it right away if, compared with before you started, you feel flatter or more depressed, things you used to enjoy stop feeling good (anhedonia), or you stop caring about them. Stop too if it winds you up instead, making you more irritable or sleepless than before, if you get dizziness or palpitations (a pounding or racing heart), if your stomach turns (nausea or loose stools), or if you're quitting something and the cravings get stronger. It's natural to want to wait the numbness out, hoping it settles like other side effects can, but don't push through it, because in rare reports it went on for weeks after people stopped taking agmatine.

marked.s: Stop agmatine right away if, compared with before you started it, you feel flatter or more numb, more depressed, unable to enjoy anything (anhedonia) or like you no longer care (apathy).

Its other side effects call for stopping too, whether that's feeling more wired than before (agitated, irritable, or sleeping badly), dizziness, palpitations (a pounding or racing heart), nausea or loose stools, or stronger cravings for whatever you're trying to quit.

The human trials only found the stomach problems, but people do get the flatness in practice, and in rare reports their loss of pleasure went on for weeks after they stopped taking agmatine, so don't push through the numbness hoping it will pass.
